data.body:
Fixes bug B-arch-guard-extras-hardcoded: test_every_extra_has_a_contract compares extra NAMES only; a package added under an existing extra in pyproject is never checked against the extras-one-adapter forbidden_modules, because _EXTRA_MODULES is hard-coded. Pre-existing (identical on main); found by the critic review of SZ-split-test_architecture_guards.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-arch-guard-extras-hardcoded --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-arch-guard-extras-hardcoded --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B-arch-guard-extras-hardcoded: test_every_extra_has_a_contract checks only hard-coded module names

data.claim: test_every_extra_has_a_contract derives extra->module names from a hard-coded _EXTRA_MODULES dict, so a package added under an existing optional-dependency extra in pyproject.toml is never checked against the extras-one-adapter forbidden_modules.
data.falsifier: Adding numpy to the rag extra would appear in the test's 'missing' output (a module not in forbidden_modules).
data.mechanism: The test's missing computation iterates only the hard-coded _EXTRA_MODULES values, never the pyproject optional-dependencies list, so the guard is blind to additions under an existing extra.
data.probe: ast-parse _EXTRA_MODULES from the test file; append numpy>=1.26 to rag in pyproject.toml; recompute missing per the test; check whether numpy appears.
data.question: Does test_every_extra_has_a_contract check packages added under an existing extra against forbidden_modules?

evidence.note: CONFIRMED (research Rc551933146). Probe: ast-parsed _EXTRA_MODULES, appended numpy>=1.26 to the existing rag extra, recomputed the test's missing dict -> all empty, 'numpy flagged? False'. Confirms the guard is blind to packages added under an existing extra because the map is hard-coded.

r-small-files: file stays ~140 lines, well under 30KB. r-reuse-core: reuses existing _contracts() helper, no duplication of the forbidden_modules parser. r-everything-configurable: no new tunable; the guard is a test. r-tell-dont-discover: helper keeps reading pyproject directly as the single source. No new rule violated.

chunk_findings.detail: This test is not a real regression guard for `test_every_extra_has_a_contract`: it only checks a locally constructed set against the global `_EXTRA_IMPORTS`, never pyproject or the actual contract test. If `numpy` is later added as a legitimate optional dependency (add `numpy` to `_EXTRA_IMPORTS` and to `forbidden_modules` so the contract test passes), this test fails because `dists - set(_EXTRA_IMPORTS)` no longer contains `numpy`. Conversely, if `test_every_extra_has_a_contract` is reverted to the old hard-coded extra-name check while `_EXTRA_IMPORTS` and `_dist_name` remain, this test still passes, so it does not prevent the original bug from returning.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:test_package_added_under_existing_extra_is_checked

chunk_findings.detail: `_dist_name` omits `@` from the separator regex, but PEP 508 also supports direct-reference requirements such as `name@url`. Given a pyproject optional dependency like `mcp@https://example.com/mcp-1.0.tar.gz`, `_dist_name` returns the whole string (or a wrong prefix if the URL contains `=`, `[`, `;`, etc.), so `dists` mismatches `_EXTRA_IMPORTS` and `test_every_extra_has_a_contract` fails/misclassifies the package even though its distribution name is `mcp`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:_dist_name

chunk_findings.detail: The new “regression” test never invokes `test_every_extra_has_a_contract` or `_contracts()`. It only builds a local `extras` dict and asserts that `"numpy"` is absent from `_EXTRA_IMPORTS`. In an environment where the actual guard is reverted to the old hard-coded `_EXTRA_MODULES` behavior while `_EXTRA_IMPORTS` remains as-is, this test still passes, so it does not actually detect the B-arch-guard-extras-hardcoded regression it claims to cover.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:test_package_added_under_existing_extra_is_checked

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test hard-codes `numpy` as the “undeclared” package, so it can fail even when the guard is working correctly. If `numpy` is later added as a legitimate optional dependency and the contract is updated properly (`_EXTRA_IMPORTS["numpy"] = "numpy"` and `numpy` included in `extras-one-adapter`’s `forbidden_modules`), then `_undeclared_imports({"rag": ["model2vec>=0.9.0", "numpy>=1.26"]})` returns `{}` and the assertion `problems == {"numpy": None}` fails. The same exact-equality check also fails if `numpy` is only partially updated (e.g. mapped but not forbidden, returning `{"numpy": "numpy"}`), making the test brittle against valid dependency/contract changes rather than isolating the regression logic.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:test_package_added_under_existing_extra_is_checked

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test hard-codes `numpy` as the undeclared package and asserts the exact result `{"numpy": None}`. When `numpy` is later legitimately added to `_EXTRA_IMPORTS` and to the `forbidden_modules` contract (a valid architecture change), `_undeclared_imports({"rag": ["model2vec>=0.9.0", "numpy>=1.26"]})` returns `{}`, so the assertion fails even though the guard is correct. This is a false-positive for a future permitted dependency; use a synthetic package name or monkeypatch the maps.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:test_package_added_under_existing_extra_is_checked

chunk_findings.detail: It still does not invoke the function that had the regression, `test_every_extra_has_a_contract`; it calls the new helper `_undeclared_imports` directly. If a future edit restores the old hard-coded `_EXTRA_MODULES` behavior in `test_every_extra_has_a_contract` while leaving `_undeclared_imports` intact, this regression test passes, so it fails to detect the exact regression it is named for.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:test_package_added_under_existing_extra_is_checked

chunk_findings.detail: The previous `dists == set(_EXTRA_IMPORTS)` check was dropped. Given a pyproject where a package is removed from all extras while its `_EXTRA_IMPORTS` entry remains (e.g., `model2vec` removed but still mapped), `_undeclared_imports` iterates only `extras.values()` and therefore returns `{}`; `test_every_extra_has_a_contract` passes with a stale import map that the old guard caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:_undeclared_imports

evidence.diff_source: delta review of 1 commit since ee04d90054

chunk_findings.detail: `_dist_name` does not treat a parenthesized version specifier as a separator. PEP 508 permits a specifier set to be wrapped in parentheses, so an optional-dependency entry such as `"rapidfuzz(>=3.14.6)"` is a valid requirement. The regex splits on the first `>` inside the parentheses and returns `"rapidfuzz("` instead of `"rapidfuzz"`, so `_EXTRA_IMPORTS.get("rapidfuzz(")` is `None` and `_unconfined` reports a false problem like `rapidfuzz(: no _EXTRA_IMPORTS entry...`, causing `test_every_extra_has_a_contract` to fail even though the package and its import are properly confined.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:_dist_name

chunk_findings.detail: `_dist_name` is not a correct PEP 508 name extractor: the split class omits `(`, so a valid optional dependency such as `"rapidfuzz(>=3.14)"` returns `"rapidfuzz("` rather than `"rapidfuzz"`, causing `_unconfined` to report `"rapidfuzz(: no _EXTRA_IMPORTS entry"` and `test_every_extra_has_a_contract` to fail even though the distribution is `rapidfuzz`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py:_dist_name

chunk_findings.detail: `_EXTRA_IMPORTS` maps each distribution to a single import string, so a distribution that installs multiple top-level import names cannot be fully represented. Given an optional dependency `{"search": ["acme>=1.0"]}` whose distribution provides both `acme` and `acme_helpers`, mapping only `"acme": "acme"` causes `_unconfined` to check only `acme`; if `acme_helpers` is absent from `forbidden_modules`, the test stays green and a package under an existing extra still slips through.

Found on TE-research.

evidence.note: CONFIRMED. Pre-fix probe: test_a_filed_anyway_add_caps_the_list_at_max_candidates FAILED (4 named candidates printed, cap=2). The settled add's success path printed data['candidates'] unbounded (assess() adds named records beyond max_candidates).
r-everything-configurable: cap uses c.cfg.dedupe.max_candidates, no magic number. r-reuse-core: reuses candidate_lines. r-small-files: files unchanged in size.

Commit 789bc9ee0. settle() caps the filed-anyway candidate list to c.cfg.dedupe.max_candidates. Regression test test_a_filed_anyway_add_caps_the_list_at_max_candidates FAILS pre-fix (4 shown) PASSES fixed (capped to 2).

chunk_findings.detail: If `max_candidates` is configured to `0`, the code still prints the advisory block. For example, with `DDFLOW_DEDUPE_MAX_CANDIDATES=0` and a non-empty `data["candidates"]`, `rows = data["candidates"][:0]` is empty, but the branch condition is based on the original candidates list, so line 218 prints `It reads like:` and line 219 prints an empty line. A user who sets the maximum to zero to suppress the advisory list still gets the header and a blank line; with a negative value, Python’s slice semantics would also fail to cap the output (e.g. `[:-1]` prints all but the last candidate).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/dedupe_flags.py:217

chunk_findings.detail: The cap uses `c.cfg.dedupe.max_candidates`, the same setting that already controls how many candidates the dedupe check returns; in the reported default TE-research run that value produced the ~12 records, so `data["candidates"]` already contains ~12 items and `data["candidates"][: c.cfg.dedupe.max_candidates]` still prints all of them. The new regression test sets `DDFLOW_DEDUPE_MAX_CANDIDATES=2` before the add, which also makes the backend return only 2 candidates, so the old code would also pass `len(ids) == 2`; the test does not demonstrate the print cap works. The fix needs an independent display cap (at most 3) or threshold filtering, and the test must keep the backend candidate limit at the default/large value while asserting the printed list is capped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/dedupe_flags.py:216

chunk_findings.detail: The fix caps the printed list at `c.cfg.dedupe.max_candidates`, but that is the same setting under which the reported “~12 unrelated records” were already produced when left at its default. An ordinary `ddflow task add T-new` with no `DDFLOW_DEDUPE_MAX_CANDIDATES` override therefore still prints up to that default number of near-duplicate lines, not the required “at most 3” behavior. The added regression test only sets `DDFLOW_DEDUPE_MAX_CANDIDATES=2`, so it never exercises the default configuration and would not catch the bug remaining in the normal path.
